title: Interjections
content: An interjection is a word that expresses some kind of emotion. It can be used as filler. Interjections do not have a grammatical function in the sentence and are not related to the other parts of the sentence. If an interjection is omitted, the sentence still makes sense. It can stand alone. - Ouch! That hurts. - Well, I need a break. - Wow! What a beautiful dress! When you are expressing a strong emotion, use an exclamation mark (!). A comma (,) can be used for a weaker emotion. Interjections do the following: 1.Express a feeling—wow, gee, oops, darn, geez, oh: - Oops, I’m sorry. That was my mistake. - Geez! Do I need to do it again? - Oh, I didn’t know that. 2.Say yes or no—yes, no, nope: - Yes! I will do it! - No, I am not going to go there. - Nope. That’s not what I want. 3.Call attention—yo, hey: - Yo, will you throw the ball back? - Hey, I just wanted to talk to you about the previous incident. 4.Indicate a pause—well, um, hmm: - Well, what I meant was nothing like that. - Um, here is our proposal. - Hmm. You really need to be on a diet. [Quiz 29.1] What should be B’s expression? A: I got a perfect score on the math exam. B: ______ (Well. Wow! or Um.) [Quiz 29.2] What should be C’s expression? C: ______! (Nope, Hey, or Geez) My computer just broke. View Answers[29.1] Wow! [29.2] Geez
